title: Employment Rate of Differently-abled in Public Service
what_it_is: Employment Rate of Differently-abled in Public Service

sections.label: Public Service differently-abled employment
sections.summary: The Public Service does not track officers recovering from mental health conditions and is committed to supporting employment of persons with special needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister (a) what is the current employment rate of the differently-abled, including persons-in-recovery from mental health conditions, in the Public Service; (b) what support structures are in place to ensure upgrading and retention of these employees; and (c) how can the Public Service as the largest employer change the mindset amongst employers to take advantage of the Open Door Programme and employment credits to support more employment of our differently-abled.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: We do not track the number of officers who are recovering from mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: As an inclusive employer, the Public Service is committed to supporting the employment of persons with special needs to take on meaningful jobs in accordance with their abilities.

sections.label: Special needs officers promoted
sections.summary: More than 70% of officers with special needs in the Civil Service had been promoted at least once.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: In fact, more than 70% of the officers with special needs in the Civil Service had been promoted at least once.

sections.label: Job fit for abilities
sections.summary: The approach is to look at what people can do and design the job scope to fit their abilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Basically, we look for a job fit, and, in line with the Member's second question, the issue is really not to look at what the people cannot do, but to look at what the people can do and then to design the job scope to fit it with the abilities of the people.

sections.label: Soft target for scheme
sections.summary: About 300 out of more than 100,000 Public Service staff are in the scheme, and a soft target is sought.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: I think it is one of the best kept secrets, and I want to honour the Minister for promoting that.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: But looking at the outcomes, which is about 300 out of more than 100,000 staff in the Public Service, I think that even the scheme must have been facing some obstacles or barriers to achieve the kind of results that we would like to see.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Even if the Public Service starts by saying, "It might end up as tokenism", there will be some who feel like they might as well make it worthwhile if they were doing it anyway.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: So, I would seek the Minister's favourable consideration to at least set a soft target.

sections.label: Available quota not hit
sections.summary: They are free from manpower constraints and have not hit anywhere near the available quota.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In fact, they are free from the manpower constraints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: They have not hit anywhere near, if you like, the pool of available quota that we have made available.

sections.label: Medical history declaration request
sections.summary: The Public Service still requests a declaration of medical history which includes mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: I may be wrong and I stand corrected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: I understand that the Public Service still requests for a declaration of medical history which includes mental health conditions.

sections.label: Minister on medical condition disclosure
sections.summary: The Minister-in-charge of the Public Service says asking about medical condition is not to blacklist or limit progression.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The greatest assurance is what I have just spoken about.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: I am the Minister-in-charge of the Public Service and I tell everyone that when we ask people for their medical condition, it is not to blacklist anybody or that this will in anyway limit their progression.

sections.label: Employment rates of persons with special needs
sections.summary: A Member asks the Minister about factors behind dismal employment rates of persons with special needs, citing job fit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: I want to ask the Minister what he thinks are the factors behind the dismal employment rates of persons with special needs, including for mental health in our Public Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: I would put it down to job fit.

sections.label: Organisations redesigning jobs
sections.summary: Organisations need to take on work and responsibility to redesign jobs, including tools and workflow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The second part, it does and it is true that organisations will need to take on a bit of work, responsibility to redesign some of the jobs from the type of tools that are being used to the workflow that is being used.

sections.label: Helping people with disability profile
sections.summary: A third factor is helping people with disability profile what they can do to bring out their best.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The third factor that I have come across is this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We also need to be able to do a much better job in helping our people with disability to profile what they can do to bring out the best in them.

sections.label: Safety exercise and HR confidential fit
sections.summary: The exercise is for team and crew safety, and HR works confidentially with a person to find the correct fit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First, I would like to reiterate that the exercise is one for the safety of the team and the crew and also to bring out the best from each.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, the correct way for us to do is that when someone comes into a job, the HR will work with them confidentially to see whether there are any limitations that that person might want to highlight, so that HR knows how best to put the person into the correct fit.

sections.label: Confidential medical history with HR
sections.summary: Medical history discussions with HR are confidential, for individual safety and appropriate job scope, and should not impede career progression.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, these are things best for us to work confidentially between the HR and the respective individuals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But I just want to say that nobody should feel that by revealing your medical record you would in any way impede your career progression.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The revelation of the discussion of one's medical history with the HR is for the purpose of the safety of the individual so that the organisation can extend the necessary help and design the appropriate job scope for the individual.
